cc @aojea @pohly 

We should probably either require migrating, or close that issue?

I think we should require migrating. It does not make sense to me to put further effort into a tool that shouldn't exist in this form.

It is in the KEP, too:
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/72341d3c572566324fffdc8409c1f1e93b354f75/keps/sig-architecture/4330-compatibility-versions/README.md#beta
> "Integrate [test/featuregate_linter](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/35488ef5c7212a3d491b86e02b1ba05dbbc4b894/test/featuregates_linter/README.md) into golangci-lint"

> I think we should require migrating. It does not make sense to me to put further effort into a tool that shouldn't exist in this form.
> 
> It is in the KEP, too: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/72341d3c572566324fffdc8409c1f1e93b354f75/keps/sig-architecture/4330-compatibility-versions/README.md#beta
> 
> > "Integrate [test/featuregate_linter](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/35488ef5c7212a3d491b86e02b1ba05dbbc4b894/test/featuregates_linter/README.md) into golangci-lint"

The verification requires knowledge of feature list from before the change. 
In addition, golangci-lint works at package level. We need to crawl the entire code base for all the features. 
I have tried it and could not find a way to make it work in lint. @pohly can you suggest a way to make it work? Thanks!

> The verification requires knowledge of feature list from before the change.

You could load and parse the on-disk file for that.

> In addition, golangci-lint works at package level. We need to crawl the entire code base for all the features.

[Facts](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis#hdr-Modular_analysis_with_Facts) might help with that. I don't know where to evaluate them, though.

If a linter really doesn't work, then at least work on how the command is described and implemented. It currently says:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/test/featuregates_linter/README.md?plain=1#L1

I don't think that we should encourage others to put their own checks into your linter. That would dilute ownership and I don't see whether it would provide sufficient advantages to justify that. If we need to run multiple such commands which can't be linters in golangci-lint, then they will still share the Go compile cache.

> > In addition, golangci-lint works at package level. We need to crawl the entire code base for all the features.
> 
> [Facts](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis#hdr-Modular_analysis_with_Facts) might help with that. I don't know where to evaluate them, though.

When it comes to the implementation details, https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis#hdr-Pass this is all we have access to regarding the files in the Analyzer, and it is only for a single package. The facts would compile the dependencies of a package first, but new features could be added inside the package level, and potentially we would have to generate a yaml file for each package to compare the differences. 
> 
> If a linter really doesn't work, then at least work on how the command is described and implemented. It currently says:
> 
> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/test/featuregates_linter/README.md?plain=1#L1
> 
> I don't think that we should encourage others to put their own checks into your linter. That would dilute ownership and I don't see whether it would provide sufficient advantages to justify that. If we need to run multiple such commands which can't be linters in golangci-lint, then they will still share the Go compile cache.

Yes, we can just limit our scripts to compat version usage. Thanks for pointing it out. 

Is it ok we remove the lint migration requirements if we do that @pohly ? Thanks!

> Is it ok we remove the lint migration requirements if we do that @pohly ? Thanks!

I'm okay with that.
+1, thank you both.

issue_context.title: [Compatibility Version]Improve hack/verify-featuregates.sh script
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?
Improve the code in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/featuregates_linter

1. since all the feature gates have been migrated to the versioned feature gate, we can remove the code to check no new feature is added to the unversioned feature gate. And prevent the usage of the unversioned `DefaultMutableFeatureGate.Add()` with a golangci-lint (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126893)
2. we need to add checks to verify that a feature can only be removed after been locked for at least 3 releases. 
    * We support EmulationVersion up to N-3. So if a feature is locked starting N, the feature gate could still be set in `BinaryVersion=N+1, EmulationVersion=N-1,-2`, and `BinaryVersion=N+2, EmulationVersion=N-1`. So the feature gate can only be removed starting the `BinaryVersion=N+3`
4. rename the go script to something more appropriate like featuregate-tracker rather than linter because it is not really a linter. 

### Why is this needed?

To improve code health and developer experience wrt Compatibility Version.

review_comments:
we might want to pull this constant out somewhere more visible or even public, for if/when this number is revisited.

NOT blocking, just a thought
Add a comment that 1.31 is when we introduced emulation version.
can you add some comments about what this function does? Thanks!
can you add a test case for removing a feature locked at 1.31?
There is a testcase "GA feature removed at threshold version" which should cover the same case.

fyi we have some exceptions: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129295, mainly around features that graduated before 1.32 and could have their gating code already removed. For those cases we allow the feature to be removed in 1.33, despite being only at n-2.

It is tricky to check whether the gated code already dropped in this script. I think we need to audit the featuregate is changed to be locked in 1.31 right? And if the featuregates already have their gated code removed, we put them in a exception list. Am I understanding correctly?

Exactly. This might also be a good list checking for 1.33 removal comments https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Akubernetes%2Fkubernetes%20%22remove%20in%201.33%22&type=code

We can proactively whitelist them or have a way for exceptions to be added, as long as the friction isn't too high. Will defer to you and @siyuanfoundation.
we can change this to `minEmulationVersion := max(currentVersion.SubtractMinor(3), 1.31)`, and if the feature is locked to default by or before `minEmulationVersion`, it is ok to remove.
@siyuanfoundation if there is still usage of the featuregate, even it is lock to GA in 1.31, is it allowed to be removed?

To make it not too confusing for users, especially because a lot of feature gates promoted in 1.31 have a `// remove in 1.33` comment, I'm inclined to just allow the removal. I don't think it's that easy to programmatically check for usage and we don't lose any behavior changes from allowing them to be removed.
Make sense. I've updated to allow the exceptions to be removed.
